overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Chris Oates, a candidate for State Representative in the 34th Middlesex District, regarding his platform and background. Oates advocated for legislative transparency, increased housing supply, and shifting the municipal tax burden to the state level to protect seniors.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Background
items.summary: Chris Oates discussed his background as a political risk analyst, his work on the 2020 Ranked Choice Voting campaign, and his motivation for seeking the open 34th Middlesex District seat.

items.title: Qualifications for State Representative
items.summary: Oates identified his primary qualifications as the ability to analyze complex policy, build statewide coalitions, and listen to diverse community perspectives.

items.title: Legislative Reform and Transparency
items.summary: The candidate proposed a 10-point plan for more competitive elections and supported open floor votes to ensure voters know where their representatives stand on key issues.

items.title: Lobbying and Campaign Finance Disclosure
items.summary: Oates supported full disclosure for all lobbying activities and noted his personal pledge not to accept PAC money to avoid conflicts of interest.

items.title: Affordable Housing Strategy
items.summary: Discussion focused on increasing the housing supply through streamlined permitting, modular construction, and enabling the development of starter homes.

items.title: Support for Term Limits
items.summary: Oates advocated for 12-year term limits in both the state House and Senate to encourage political churn and force more competitive open-seat elections.

items.title: Senior Citizens and Fiscal Reform
items.summary: Oates proposed shifting more municipal funding burdens to the state level to reduce reliance on local property taxes, which often strain seniors on fixed incomes.
